cohort: The study participants consisted of 528 children (72.7% male), including 174 with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), 178 their typically developed siblings (TDS), and 176 typically developed children from the general population (TDP).
finding: Abnormal fetal head growth is a familial trait of ASD, modulated by sex, and associated with the severity of the disorder, suggesting it could serve as an early biomarker for ASD.
cross-section timing: Measurements were taken during the second and third trimesters of gestation.
